/oneOf/4/properties/level.label: Compression level
/oneOf/4/properties/level.explanation: Higher levels generally spend more CPU and memory to reduce file size, with identical decoded content. Zstandard permits 1–22; compatibility codecs permit 1–9. Use fast acceleration instead of an explicit level when speed dominates.
/oneOf/4/properties/level.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 3. Higher levels generally spend more CPU and memory to reduce file size, with identical decoded content. Zstandard permits 1–22; compatibility codecs permit 1–9. Use fast acceleration instead of an explicit level when speed dominates.

/oneOf/4/properties/fast.label: Fast-mode acceleration
/oneOf/4/properties/fast.explanation: A positive value selects the native fast mode; larger values favour speed over compressed size. Zero uses the level. Supplying both a positive acceleration and an explicit level is refused.
/oneOf/4/properties/fast.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. A positive value selects the native fast mode; larger values favour speed over compressed size. Zero uses the level. Supplying both a positive acceleration and an explicit level is refused.

/oneOf/4/properties/threads.label: Compression workers
/oneOf/4/properties/threads.explanation: One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.
/oneOf/4/properties/threads.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.

/oneOf/4/properties/singleThread.label: Single-thread I/O
/oneOf/4/properties/singleThread.explanation: Use the native strictly single-thread implementation. It requires one worker and cannot be combined with rsyncable compression.
/oneOf/4/properties/singleThread.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Use the native strictly single-thread implementation. It requires one worker and cannot be combined with rsyncable compression.

/oneOf/4/properties/checksum.label: Content checksum
/oneOf/4/properties/checksum.explanation: Write the low 32 bits of XXH64 over decoded content into every Zstandard frame. The host independently recomputes it after fresh decoding. This detects accidental corruption; it is not an authenticity signature.
/oneOf/4/properties/checksum.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. Write the low 32 bits of XXH64 over decoded content into every Zstandard frame. The host independently recomputes it after fresh decoding. This detects accidental corruption; it is not an authenticity signature.

/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryID.label: Write dictionary identifier
/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryID.explanation: Include the dictionary numeric ID in frame headers. Turning this off does not embed the dictionary or remove its dependency; retain the exact captured dictionary.
/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryID.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. Include the dictionary numeric ID in frame headers. Turning this off does not embed the dictionary or remove its dependency; retain the exact captured dictionary.

/oneOf/4/properties/longWindowLog.label: Long-distance window log
/oneOf/4/properties/longWindowLog.explanation: Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.
/oneOf/4/properties/longWindowLog.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.

/oneOf/4/properties/rsyncable.label: Transfer-friendly boundaries
/oneOf/4/properties/rsyncable.explanation: Enable native rsyncable block selection to reduce retransmission after file changes. It trades some compression efficiency for more stable boundaries and requires the worker-based implementation.
/oneOf/4/properties/rsyncable.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Enable native rsyncable block selection to reduce retransmission after file changes. It trades some compression efficiency for more stable boundaries and requires the worker-based implementation.

/oneOf/4/properties/literals.label: Literal coding policy
/oneOf/4/properties/literals.explanation: Let Zstandard choose, force compressed literals, or force raw literals. This controls unreferenced bytes inside blocks rather than whether the entire file is compressed.
/oneOf/4/properties/literals.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "automatic". Let Zstandard choose, force compressed literals, or force raw literals. This controls unreferenced bytes inside blocks rather than whether the entire file is compressed.

/oneOf/4/properties/chunkBytes.label: Independent chunk size
/oneOf/4/properties/chunkBytes.explanation: Zero creates one frame. A positive byte count cuts the captured source into independently compressed frames; at most 256 are permitted. This aids bounded access but may reduce compression across boundaries.
/oneOf/4/properties/chunkBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero creates one frame. A positive byte count cuts the captured source into independently compressed frames; at most 256 are permitted. This aids bounded access but may reduce compression across boundaries.

/oneOf/4/properties/streamInput.label: Standard-input compression
/oneOf/4/properties/streamInput.explanation: Feed finite captured content through standard input. Its frame omits content size unless an exact pledgedBytes value is supplied. Actual decoded bytes remain bounded and checked.
/oneOf/4/properties/streamInput.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Feed finite captured content through standard input. Its frame omits content size unless an exact pledgedBytes value is supplied. Actual decoded bytes remain bounded and checked.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning.label: Expert compression tuning
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning.explanation: Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use {}. Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/wi.label: History window log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/wi.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match history window in bytes. This expert override changes the level preset and must agree with an explicitly enabled long-distance window.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ch.label: Match-chain table log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ch.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match-chain table size. Requires an explicit non-fast strategy, including doubleFast, which uses it for the secondary probe table. The native fast strategy ignores this control.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ha.label: Match hash table log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ha.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the native match hash table size. Larger tables reduce collisions while increasing memory. Start from the level preset unless tuning representative data.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/se.label: Match search effort log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/se.explanation: Base-two logarithm of native search attempts. Requires explicit greedy, lazy, lazy2, btlazy2, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy; fast/doubleFast ignore this control. More search can consume substantially more CPU.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/mi.label: Strategy-valid minimum match
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/mi.explanation: Minimum searched match length. Values 4–6 work across strategies. Three requires explicit btopt, btultra or btultra2; seven requires explicit fast. Other combinations are refused because native Zstandard clamps them, and an unspecified preset depends on input size.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ta.label: Strategy-dependent target length
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ta.explanation: A nonzero target length requires explicit fast, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy. Other strategies do not consume this control and are refused rather than silently ignoring it.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/st.label: Match strategy
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/st.explanation: Select a named native strategy from fast through btultra2. More elaborate strategies generally spend more CPU searching for smaller encodings; every result must still restore identical bytes.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ov.label: Worker history overlap
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ov.explanation: Native overlap log 0–9 controls how much preceding history is reused by compression workers. Zero selects automatic overlap. Larger values improve cross-job matching at extra processing cost; unavailable in strict single-thread mode.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance insertion rate
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm controlling how sparsely long-distance matches enter the hash table. Requires explicit long-distance matching; larger values reduce table insertion work.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance hash table log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance match-table entries. Requires longWindowLog and determines memory demand independently of the ordinary match-finder hash table.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance minimum match
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Minimum match length used by the long-distance matcher. Requires longWindowLog and affects long-range match selectivity rather than ordinary short-match length.

/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance bucket log
/oneOf/4/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance entries per bucket. Requires longWindowLog and must not exceed the long-distance hash-table log.

/oneOf/4/properties/dictionary.label: Captured dictionary
/oneOf/4/properties/dictionary.explanation: Select exact trained dictionary bytes or raw history bytes using dictionaryMode. A numeric dictionary ID is not a cryptographic identity. A dictionary and a delta reference are alternative dependency mechanisms. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryMode.label: Dictionary representation
/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryMode.explanation: Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.
/oneOf/4/properties/dictionaryMode.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "trained". Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.

/oneOf/4/properties/contentSize.label: Frame content size
/oneOf/4/properties/contentSize.explanation: Automatic includes a known file size and omits an unknown stream size. Omit suppresses the frame size. Require needs an exact pledgedBytes value for a standard-input stream. Actual decoded output remains bounded in every mode.
/oneOf/4/properties/contentSize.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "automatic". Automatic includes a known file size and omits an unknown stream size. Omit suppresses the frame size. Require needs an exact pledgedBytes value for a standard-input stream. Actual decoded output remains bounded in every mode.

/oneOf/4/properties/pledgedBytes.label: Exact stream byte count
/oneOf/4/properties/pledgedBytes.explanation: Exact total source bytes for one standard-input frame. The captured byte count must match before native execution. A pledge cannot be combined with chunking or an approximate size hint.

/oneOf/4/properties/sizeHintBytes.label: Approximate stream size
/oneOf/4/properties/sizeHintBytes.explanation: Hint used to select compression parameters for a standard-input stream. It does not assert the actual size or remove decoded-output limits. Use pledgedBytes when an exact frame size is required.

/oneOf/4/properties/targetBlockBytes.label: Approximate encoded block target
/oneOf/4/properties/targetBlockBytes.explanation: Zero uses the native default. A positive value asks for an approximate compressed block size, 64–131072 bytes. It is a compression target rather than an exact block-size or random-access guarantee.
/oneOf/4/properties/targetBlockBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero uses the native default. A positive value asks for an approximate compressed block size, 64–131072 bytes. It is a compression target rather than an exact block-size or random-access guarantee.

/oneOf/4/properties/jobBytes.label: Worker job size
/oneOf/4/properties/jobBytes.explanation: Zero uses automatic worker scheduling. A positive value requires an explicit tuning.windowLog or longWindowLog and covers at least 512 KiB and the selected history overlap. Automatic overlap reserves the full window so native scheduling cannot silently increase an undersized request. It requires worker-based I/O. Delta encoding derives its window from captured sizes and refuses explicit job-size overrides.
/oneOf/4/properties/jobBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero uses automatic worker scheduling. A positive value requires an explicit tuning.windowLog or longWindowLog and covers at least 512 KiB and the selected history overlap. Automatic overlap reserves the full window so native scheduling cannot silently increase an undersized request. It requires worker-based I/O. Delta encoding derives its window from captured sizes and refuses explicit job-size overrides.

/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive.label: Adaptive compression range
/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive.explanation: Let native Zstandard adjust compression effort within named level bounds as throughput changes. Bounds must include the initial level and require worker-based compression. Native adaptation is not reproducible; verification proves content and frame policy, not the historical level schedule.

/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.label: Lowest adaptive level
/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.explanation: Lower bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must be no greater than the initial compression level or the maximum bound.
/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. Lower bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must be no greater than the initial compression level or the maximum bound.

/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.label: Highest adaptive level
/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.explanation: Upper bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must include the initial level. Values above 19 enable native ultra compression and can require substantially more memory.
/oneOf/4/properties/adaptive/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 19. Upper bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must include the initial level. Values above 19 enable native ultra compression and can require substantially more memory.

/oneOf/4/properties/reference.explanation: Select the earlier complete byte sequence used by delta compression. Restoration needs the exact same reference; it is retained as a captured dependency. /oneOf/7.label: benchmark
/oneOf/7.explanation: Measure native in-memory compression and decompression throughput over captured representative content, with independently checked sizes and round trips.

/oneOf/7/properties/version.label: Document contract
/oneOf/7/properties/version.explanation: Selects this finite compression document contract. Keep this value while editing parameters; it is not the native executable version.

/oneOf/7/properties/operation.label: Compression task
/oneOf/7/properties/operation.explanation: Choose compression, restoration, frame inspection, dictionary training, snapshot delta, ordered frame join, profile comparison or native throughput measurement.

/oneOf/7/properties/source.label: Input file
/oneOf/7/properties/source.explanation: Absolute local regular file to capture. Compression and comparison treat it as original bytes; restoration and frame inspection treat it as a compressed stream. Dictionary inspection treats it as exact dictionary bytes. Changing bytes at the same path invalidates reuse. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/7/properties/firstLevel.label: First benchmark level
/oneOf/7/properties/firstLevel.explanation: First compression level in the native benchmark range, 1–22. At most four consecutive levels may be measured; each result is independently reconstructed and restored.
/oneOf/7/properties/firstLevel.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. First compression level in the native benchmark range, 1–22. At most four consecutive levels may be measured; each result is independently reconstructed and restored.

/oneOf/7/properties/lastLevel.label: Last benchmark level
/oneOf/7/properties/lastLevel.explanation: Last compression level, at least firstLevel and at most three levels higher. Higher levels can require more time and memory even for a short measurement interval.
/oneOf/7/properties/lastLevel.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 3. Last compression level, at least firstLevel and at most three levels higher. Higher levels can require more time and memory even for a short measurement interval.

/oneOf/7/properties/minimumSeconds.label: Minimum measurement interval
/oneOf/7/properties/minimumSeconds.explanation: Native minimum measurement seconds per compression/decompression test, 1–3. Total elapsed time includes every level, fresh verification and process startup. Later verification cannot authenticate historical measured throughput.
/oneOf/7/properties/minimumSeconds.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. Native minimum measurement seconds per compression/decompression test, 1–3. Total elapsed time includes every level, fresh verification and process startup. Later verification cannot authenticate historical measured throughput.

/oneOf/7/properties/benchmarkBlockBytes.label: Independent benchmark blocks
/oneOf/7/properties/benchmarkBlockBytes.explanation: Zero measures the whole captured input. A positive size of at least 1024 bytes divides it into independent compression blocks, at most 256. Sizes are checked against separately created CLI frames; this is distinct from the codec internal block target.
/oneOf/7/properties/benchmarkBlockBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero measures the whole captured input. A positive size of at least 1024 bytes divides it into independent compression blocks, at most 256. Sizes are checked against separately created CLI frames; this is distinct from the codec internal block target.

/oneOf/7/properties/threads.label: Compression workers
/oneOf/7/properties/threads.explanation: One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.
/oneOf/7/properties/threads.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.

/oneOf/7/properties/dictionary.label: Captured dictionary
/oneOf/7/properties/dictionary.explanation: Select exact trained dictionary bytes or raw history bytes using dictionaryMode. A numeric dictionary ID is not a cryptographic identity. A dictionary and a delta reference are alternative dependency mechanisms. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/7/properties/dictionaryMode.label: Dictionary representation
/oneOf/7/properties/dictionaryMode.explanation: Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.
/oneOf/7/properties/dictionaryMode.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "trained". Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning.label: Expert compression tuning
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning.explanation: Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use {}. Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/wi.label: History window log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/wi.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match history window in bytes. This expert override changes the level preset and must agree with an explicitly enabled long-distance window.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ch.label: Match-chain table log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ch.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match-chain table size. Requires an explicit non-fast strategy, including doubleFast, which uses it for the secondary probe table. The native fast strategy ignores this control.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ha.label: Match hash table log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ha.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the native match hash table size. Larger tables reduce collisions while increasing memory. Start from the level preset unless tuning representative data.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/se.label: Match search effort log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/se.explanation: Base-two logarithm of native search attempts. Requires explicit greedy, lazy, lazy2, btlazy2, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy; fast/doubleFast ignore this control. More search can consume substantially more CPU.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/mi.label: Strategy-valid minimum match
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/mi.explanation: Minimum searched match length. Values 4–6 work across strategies. Three requires explicit btopt, btultra or btultra2; seven requires explicit fast. Other combinations are refused because native Zstandard clamps them, and an unspecified preset depends on input size.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ta.label: Strategy-dependent target length
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ta.explanation: A nonzero target length requires explicit fast, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy. Other strategies do not consume this control and are refused rather than silently ignoring it.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/st.label: Match strategy
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/st.explanation: Select a named native strategy from fast through btultra2. More elaborate strategies generally spend more CPU searching for smaller encodings; every result must still restore identical bytes.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ov.label: Worker history overlap
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ov.explanation: Native overlap log 0–9 controls how much preceding history is reused by compression workers. Zero selects automatic overlap. Larger values improve cross-job matching at extra processing cost; unavailable in strict single-thread mode.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance insertion rate
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm controlling how sparsely long-distance matches enter the hash table. Requires explicit long-distance matching; larger values reduce table insertion work.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance hash table log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance match-table entries. Requires longWindowLog and determines memory demand independently of the ordinary match-finder hash table.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance minimum match
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Minimum match length used by the long-distance matcher. Requires longWindowLog and affects long-range match selectivity rather than ordinary short-match length.

/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.label: Long-distance bucket log
/oneOf/7/properties/tuning/properties/ld.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance entries per bucket. Requires longWindowLog and must not exceed the long-distance hash-table log.

/oneOf/7/properties/longWindowLog.label: Long-distance window log
/oneOf/7/properties/longWindowLog.explanation: Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.
/oneOf/7/properties/longWindowLog.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.

/oneOf/10.label: compressFiles
/oneOf/10.explanation: Compress a reusable named or recursively selected file set, preserving relative names with bounded captured inputs and collision checks.

/oneOf/10/properties/version.label: Document contract

/oneOf/10/properties/operation.label: Compression task
/oneOf/10/properties/operation.explanation: Choose compression, restoration, frame inspection, dictionary training, snapshot delta, ordered frame join, profile comparison or native throughput measurement.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet.label: Captured file selection
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet.explanation: Choose a root directory with relative-name filters or an explicit list of named files. The finite selection is retained before native work; output relative names must be distinct and cannot traverse directories.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Source directory
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Absolute canonical directory to examine before capture. Use include and exclude to select relative names, with at most 32 regular files, 4096 examined entries and 16 path components. Publish outside this directory. In a workflow, this also accepts a complete pinned directory snapshot; selection examines only captured data, with the same recursion, file and byte limits.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Explicit named inputs
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: List absolute source paths and distinct relative names. These names determine the publication tree, so files from different directories can share a basename when their relative names differ. Directory filters cannot accompany this list.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Explicit named inputs
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. List absolute source paths and distinct relative names. These names determine the publication tree, so files from different directories can share a basename when their relative names differ. Directory filters cannot accompany this list.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Input file
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Absolute local regular file to capture. Compression and comparison treat it as original bytes; restoration and frame inspection treat it as a compressed stream. Dictionary inspection treats it as exact dictionary bytes. Changing bytes at the same path invalidates reuse. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative publication name
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Use a relative UTF-8 file name such as run-A/results.bin, without dot traversal, backslashes or control characters. Names permit 1024 bytes and 255 bytes per component; the final output leaf must leave 32 bytes for shared metadata/atomic publication. Compression appends its codec suffix; restoration removes recognised suffixes. File/directory, case and metadata-companion collisions are refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Include nested directories
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: True examines nested directories under the selected root. False examines only immediate files. Symbolic links are never followed, and selected links are refused.
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. True examines nested directories under the selected root. False examines only immediate files. Symbolic links are never followed, and selected links are refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to include
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use ["*"]. One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to include
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to exclude
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use []. Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.

/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to exclude
/oneOf/10/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.

/oneOf/10/properties/format.label: Compressed format
/oneOf/10/properties/format.explanation: Zstandard is the default. gzip, xz, lzma and lz4 provide compatibility with other readers; Zstandard-only controls are refused for those formats.
/oneOf/10/properties/format.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "zstd". Zstandard is the default. gzip, xz, lzma and lz4 provide compatibility with other readers; Zstandard-only controls are refused for those formats.

/oneOf/10/properties/level.label: Compression level
/oneOf/10/properties/level.explanation: Higher levels generally spend more CPU and memory to reduce file size, with identical decoded content. Zstandard permits 1–22; compatibility codecs permit 1–9. Use fast acceleration instead of an explicit level when speed dominates.
/oneOf/10/properties/level.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 3. Higher levels generally spend more CPU and memory to reduce file size, with identical decoded content. Zstandard permits 1–22; compatibility codecs permit 1–9. Use fast acceleration instead of an explicit level when speed dominates.

/oneOf/10/properties/fast.label: Fast-mode acceleration
/oneOf/10/properties/fast.explanation: A positive value selects the native fast mode; larger values favour speed over compressed size. Zero uses the level. Supplying both a positive acceleration and an explicit level is refused.
/oneOf/10/properties/fast.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. A positive value selects the native fast mode; larger values favour speed over compressed size. Zero uses the level. Supplying both a positive acceleration and an explicit level is refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/threads.label: Compression workers
/oneOf/10/properties/threads.explanation: One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.
/oneOf/10/properties/threads.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O.

/oneOf/10/properties/singleThread.label: Single-thread I/O
/oneOf/10/properties/singleThread.explanation: Use the native strictly single-thread implementation. It requires one worker and cannot be combined with rsyncable compression.
/oneOf/10/properties/singleThread.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Use the native strictly single-thread implementation. It requires one worker and cannot be combined with rsyncable compression.

/oneOf/10/properties/checksum.label: Content checksum
/oneOf/10/properties/checksum.explanation: Write the low 32 bits of XXH64 over decoded content into every Zstandard frame. The host independently recomputes it after fresh decoding. This detects accidental corruption; it is not an authenticity signature.
/oneOf/10/properties/checksum.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. Write the low 32 bits of XXH64 over decoded content into every Zstandard frame. The host independently recomputes it after fresh decoding. This detects accidental corruption; it is not an authenticity signature.

/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryID.label: Write dictionary identifier
/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryID.explanation: Include the dictionary numeric ID in frame headers. Turning this off does not embed the dictionary or remove its dependency; retain the exact captured dictionary.
/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryID.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. Include the dictionary numeric ID in frame headers. Turning this off does not embed the dictionary or remove its dependency; retain the exact captured dictionary.

/oneOf/10/properties/longWindowLog.label: Long-distance window log
/oneOf/10/properties/longWindowLog.explanation: Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.
/oneOf/10/properties/longWindowLog.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory.

/oneOf/10/properties/rsyncable.label: Transfer-friendly boundaries
/oneOf/10/properties/rsyncable.explanation: Enable native rsyncable block selection to reduce retransmission after file changes. It trades some compression efficiency for more stable boundaries and requires the worker-based implementation.
/oneOf/10/properties/rsyncable.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Enable native rsyncable block selection to reduce retransmission after file changes. It trades some compression efficiency for more stable boundaries and requires the worker-based implementation.

/oneOf/10/properties/literals.label: Literal coding policy
/oneOf/10/properties/literals.explanation: Let Zstandard choose, force compressed literals, or force raw literals. This controls unreferenced bytes inside blocks rather than whether the entire file is compressed.
/oneOf/10/properties/literals.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "automatic". Let Zstandard choose, force compressed literals, or force raw literals. This controls unreferenced bytes inside blocks rather than whether the entire file is compressed.

/oneOf/10/properties/chunkBytes.label: Independent chunk size
/oneOf/10/properties/chunkBytes.explanation: Zero creates one frame. A positive byte count cuts the captured source into independently compressed frames; at most 256 are permitted. This aids bounded access but may reduce compression across boundaries.
/oneOf/10/properties/chunkBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero creates one frame. A positive byte count cuts the captured source into independently compressed frames; at most 256 are permitted. This aids bounded access but may reduce compression across boundaries.

/oneOf/10/properties/streamInput.label: Standard-input compression
/oneOf/10/properties/streamInput.explanation: Feed finite captured content through standard input. Its frame omits content size unless an exact pledgedBytes value is supplied. Actual decoded bytes remain bounded and checked.
/oneOf/10/properties/streamInput.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use false. Feed finite captured content through standard input. Its frame omits content size unless an exact pledgedBytes value is supplied. Actual decoded bytes remain bounded and checked.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning.label: Expert compression tuning
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning.explanation: Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use {}. Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/w.label: History window log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/w.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match history window in bytes. This expert override changes the level preset and must agree with an explicitly enabled long-distance window.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/c.label: Match-chain table log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/c.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the match-chain table size. Requires an explicit non-fast strategy, including doubleFast, which uses it for the secondary probe table. The native fast strategy ignores this control.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/h.label: Match hash table log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/h.explanation: Base-two logarithm of the native match hash table size. Larger tables reduce collisions while increasing memory. Start from the level preset unless tuning representative data.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/s.label: Match search effort log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/s.explanation: Base-two logarithm of native search attempts. Requires explicit greedy, lazy, lazy2, btlazy2, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy; fast/doubleFast ignore this control. More search can consume substantially more CPU.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/m.label: Strategy-valid minimum match
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/m.explanation: Minimum searched match length. Values 4–6 work across strategies. Three requires explicit btopt, btultra or btultra2; seven requires explicit fast. Other combinations are refused because native Zstandard clamps them, and an unspecified preset depends on input size.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/t.label: Strategy-dependent target length
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/t.explanation: A nonzero target length requires explicit fast, btopt, btultra or btultra2 strategy. Other strategies do not consume this control and are refused rather than silently ignoring it.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/s.label: Match strategy
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/s.explanation: Select a named native strategy from fast through btultra2. More elaborate strategies generally spend more CPU searching for smaller encodings; every result must still restore identical bytes.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/o.label: Worker history overlap
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/o.explanation: Native overlap log 0–9 controls how much preceding history is reused by compression workers. Zero selects automatic overlap. Larger values improve cross-job matching at extra processing cost; unavailable in strict single-thread mode.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.label: Long-distance insertion rate
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.explanation: Logarithm controlling how sparsely long-distance matches enter the hash table. Requires explicit long-distance matching; larger values reduce table insertion work.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.label: Long-distance hash table log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance match-table entries. Requires longWindowLog and determines memory demand independently of the ordinary match-finder hash table.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.label: Long-distance minimum match
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.explanation: Minimum match length used by the long-distance matcher. Requires longWindowLog and affects long-range match selectivity rather than ordinary short-match length.

/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.label: Long-distance bucket log
/oneOf/10/properties/tuning/properties/l.explanation: Logarithm of long-distance entries per bucket. Requires longWindowLog and must not exceed the long-distance hash-table log.

/oneOf/10/properties/dictionary.label: Captured dictionary
/oneOf/10/properties/dictionary.explanation: Select exact trained dictionary bytes or raw history bytes using dictionaryMode. A numeric dictionary ID is not a cryptographic identity. A dictionary and a delta reference are alternative dependency mechanisms. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryMode.label: Dictionary representation
/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryMode.explanation: Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.
/oneOf/10/properties/dictionaryMode.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "trained". Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.

/oneOf/10/properties/contentSize.label: Frame content size
/oneOf/10/properties/contentSize.explanation: Automatic includes a known file size and omits an unknown stream size. Omit suppresses the frame size. Require needs an exact pledgedBytes value for a standard-input stream. Actual decoded output remains bounded in every mode.
/oneOf/10/properties/contentSize.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "automatic". Automatic includes a known file size and omits an unknown stream size. Omit suppresses the frame size. Require needs an exact pledgedBytes value for a standard-input stream. Actual decoded output remains bounded in every mode.

/oneOf/10/properties/sizeHintBytes.label: Approximate stream size
/oneOf/10/properties/sizeHintBytes.explanation: Hint used to select compression parameters for a standard-input stream. It does not assert the actual size or remove decoded-output limits. Use pledgedBytes when an exact frame size is required.

/oneOf/10/properties/targetBlockBytes.label: Approximate encoded block target
/oneOf/10/properties/targetBlockBytes.explanation: Zero uses the native default. A positive value asks for an approximate compressed block size, 64–131072 bytes. It is a compression target rather than an exact block-size or random-access guarantee.
/oneOf/10/properties/targetBlockBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero uses the native default. A positive value asks for an approximate compressed block size, 64–131072 bytes. It is a compression target rather than an exact block-size or random-access guarantee.

/oneOf/10/properties/jobBytes.label: Worker job size
/oneOf/10/properties/jobBytes.explanation: Zero uses automatic worker scheduling. A positive value requires an explicit tuning.windowLog or longWindowLog and covers at least 512 KiB and the selected history overlap. Automatic overlap reserves the full window so native scheduling cannot silently increase an undersized request. It requires worker-based I/O. Delta encoding derives its window from captured sizes and refuses explicit job-size overrides.
/oneOf/10/properties/jobBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 0. Zero uses automatic worker scheduling. A positive value requires an explicit tuning.windowLog or longWindowLog and covers at least 512 KiB and the selected history overlap. Automatic overlap reserves the full window so native scheduling cannot silently increase an undersized request. It requires worker-based I/O. Delta encoding derives its window from captured sizes and refuses explicit job-size overrides.

/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive.label: Adaptive compression range
/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive.explanation: Let native Zstandard adjust compression effort within named level bounds as throughput changes. Bounds must include the initial level and require worker-based compression. Native adaptation is not reproducible; verification proves content and frame policy, not the historical level schedule.

/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.label: Lowest adaptive level
/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.explanation: Lower bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must be no greater than the initial compression level or the maximum bound.
/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 1. Lower bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must be no greater than the initial compression level or the maximum bound.

/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.label: Highest adaptive level
/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.explanation: Upper bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must include the initial level. Values above 19 enable native ultra compression and can require substantially more memory.
/oneOf/10/properties/adaptive/properties.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 19. Upper bound on native adaptive compression effort. It must include the initial level. Values above 19 enable native ultra compression and can require substantially more memory.

/oneOf/11/properties/version.label: Document contract
/oneOf/11/properties/version.explanation: Selects this finite compression document contract. Keep this value while editing parameters; it is not the native executable version.

/oneOf/11/properties/operation.label: Compression task
/oneOf/11/properties/operation.explanation: Choose compression, restoration, frame inspection, dictionary training, snapshot delta, ordered frame join, profile comparison or native throughput measurement.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet.label: Captured file selection
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet.explanation: Choose a root directory with relative-name filters or an explicit list of named files. The finite selection is retained before native work; output relative names must be distinct and cannot traverse directories.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Source directory
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Absolute canonical directory to examine before capture. Use include and exclude to select relative names, with at most 32 regular files, 4096 examined entries and 16 path components. Publish outside this directory. In a workflow, this also accepts a complete pinned directory snapshot; selection examines only captured data, with the same recursion, file and byte limits.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Explicit named inputs
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: List absolute source paths and distinct relative names. These names determine the publication tree, so files from different directories can share a basename when their relative names differ. Directory filters cannot accompany this list.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Explicit named inputs
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. List absolute source paths and distinct relative names. These names determine the publication tree, so files from different directories can share a basename when their relative names differ. Directory filters cannot accompany this list.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Input file
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Absolute local regular file to capture. Compression and comparison treat it as original bytes; restoration and frame inspection treat it as a compressed stream. Dictionary inspection treats it as exact dictionary bytes. Changing bytes at the same path invalidates reuse. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative publication name
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Use a relative UTF-8 file name such as run-A/results.bin, without dot traversal, backslashes or control characters. Names permit 1024 bytes and 255 bytes per component; the final output leaf must leave 32 bytes for shared metadata/atomic publication. Compression appends its codec suffix; restoration removes recognised suffixes. File/directory, case and metadata-companion collisions are refused.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Include nested directories
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: True examines nested directories under the selected root. False examines only immediate files. Symbolic links are never followed, and selected links are refused.
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. True examines nested directories under the selected root. False examines only immediate files. Symbolic links are never followed, and selected links are refused.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to include
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use ["*"]. One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to include
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. One to sixteen case-sensitive shell-style name patterns, interpreted by the host without a shell. Patterns match the whole relative path; * also matches directory separators. The default * includes every regular file.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to exclude
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use []. Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.

/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.label: Relative names to exclude
/oneOf/11/properties/fileSet/properties/.explanation: One captured member in this ordered list. Case-sensitive relative-name patterns to omit after inclusion. Matching directories are pruned before traversal, and every retained name must also obey all excluded ancestor directories. Empty excludes nothing; excluded symbolic links are ignored without following them.

/oneOf/11/properties/dictionary.label: Captured dictionary
/oneOf/11/properties/dictionary.explanation: Select exact trained dictionary bytes or raw history bytes using dictionaryMode. A numeric dictionary ID is not a cryptographic identity. A dictionary and a delta reference are alternative dependency mechanisms. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused.

/oneOf/11/properties/dictionaryMode.label: Dictionary representation
/oneOf/11/properties/dictionaryMode.explanation: Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.
/oneOf/11/properties/dictionaryMode.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use "trained". Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration.

/oneOf/11/properties/maxDecodedBytes.label: Decoded output limit
/oneOf/11/properties/maxDecodedBytes.explanation: Maximum actual decoded byte count, not merely the declared header size. It also constrains unknown-size streams and concatenated output. Zero permits only empty decoded content.
/oneOf/11/properties/maxDecodedBytes.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use 67108864. Maximum actual decoded byte count, not merely the declared header size. It also constrains unknown-size streams and concatenated output. Zero permits only empty decoded content.

/oneOf/11/properties/sparseOutput.label: Sparse restored file
/oneOf/11/properties/sparseOutput.explanation: Allow the native decoder to represent zero runs as filesystem holes. False requests ordinary writes. Content and logical byte count are verified; physical allocation depends on the destination filesystem.
/oneOf/11/properties/sparseOutput.defaultMeaning: When omitted, use true. Allow the native decoder to represent zero runs as filesystem holes. False requests ordinary writes. Content and logical byte count are verified; physical allocation depends on the destination filesystem.
